correctness.rationale: For n>=6, every path of length three along the cycle is geodesic, so feasible sets are exactly binary cyclic words with at most two ones per four-window. Window averaging proves the optimum floor(n/2). For optimal sets the cyclic positive gaps satisfy g_i+g_(i+1)>=4. The slack s_i=g_i+g_(i+1)-4 sums to zero for even n and two for odd n. Solving its cyclic linear equations classifies every possible gap tuple, yielding the four exact counts. A double count by starting selected vertex gives n/m times the gap-tuple number; rotational stabilizers are addressed separately. Actual code `verify.py` independently checked direct distance membership on 13,472 candidate subsets, all 2,786,632 optimum-size candidates through n=23, rotation counts through n=18, and transfer counts through n=120. No finite test substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2020 original general d-position paper gives cycle maximum sizes and a general set-characterization (Proposition 3.3, Theorem 4.1), and the 2024 k-general d-position paper supplies a maximally even extremizer and the general optimum number (Theorem 4.6). Neither inspected primary treatment counts all optimal sets or computes the mod-four number of their rotation classes. The 2024 maximal-evenness paper studies energy-minimizing sets, a different subfamily. Targeted mathematical-record and literature searches for exact cyclic four-window counts did not retrieve a covering result. The older general characterization provides feasible-set conditions, not the newly proved closed optimizer census. Residual classical cyclic-word priority risk is explicitly retained.

Published mathematical indexing and web retrieval are not exhaustive; no claim of absolute publication priority.

value.rationale: The cited research settles a scalar maximum and supplies an even witness but leaves the multiplicity and cyclic symmetry of all maxima unresolved in those texts. The exact count has a sharp modulus-four transition (only 2 or 6 labeled optima at even orders versus quadratic growth at odd orders), and the odd-order number of rotation classes grows unboundedly. This is a natural equality-case statistic and shows that maximal-evenness is not a complete structural classification of all optimum sets. The target was motivated before computation; it is not a generic parameter substitution or known-table reprint.
